newsitem.title: UK: Tesco unlikely buyer for Littlewoods chain.
newsitem.headline: Tesco unlikely buyer for Littlewoods chain.

text.p: British supermarket group Tesco Plc said on Tuesday it was unlikely to buy the 135 shops put up for sale by privately-owned Littlewoods last month.
At a press conference, chairman Lord MacLaurin said the company had asked for information on the stores but felt it had a lot on after buying the Irish supermarkets of Associated British Foods (ABF).

Littlewoods said in March that it was looking into the possibility of selling its stores division, estimated to be worth over 500 million stg, and Tesco was tipped along with rival ASDA as a possible buyer.
Tesco also ruled out any major involvement in selling electricity and gas once these markets are opened up to competition in 1998.
"We have a very big business here to run, (electricity and gas) could be a part but there are no current plans...it is never likely to become that significant," chief executive Terry Leahy said.

He added that Tesco's plans to open just two Express format stores, which stand by petrol stations, in the coming year compared with seven last year, reflected the impact of a fierce petrol price war in the first half.
"We've just been through the biggest price war (for some years), it seemed sensible to pause and just bed in," Leahy said.
Tesco earlier reported annual pre-tax profits up 10 percent as expected to 750 million stg and said it would pay out a total dividend of 10.35 pence, compared with 9.6 pence a year ago.
